To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we developed a paleoclimate record of lake sediment from Lake Towuti using VNIR reflectance, and (2) this record shows the relative proportion of serpentine and kaolinite increases during the Last Glacial Maxium, indicating that lake levels were lower.

we have developed a 40,000 year record of lake sediment from Lake Towuti in Indonesia that records past environmental change and that we have shown that visible and near-infrared reflectance spectroscopy can be used to interpret this record.
VNIR reflectances can be used to identify and track the evolution of Al-phyllo silicates in lake sedimentary records.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and applying a new method for reconstructing paleoenvironmental conditions on Earth from lake sediment records and applying this approach to paleolake deposits preserved on Mars.
developing new approaches for characterizing paleoclimate from sedimentary archives, with the goal of applying these techniques to paleolake deposits preserved in the geological record of Mars.

developing a methodology for using VNIR reflectance data from sedimentary rocks to reconstruct past environmental conditions on both Earth and Mars, with a specific focus on the paleolake environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VNIR reflectivity spectroscopy is a rapid, non-destructive, and effective way for developing paleoenvironments.
VNIR reflectivity spectroscopy is a powerful tool for reconstructing paleoenvironmental conditions on Earth and potentially on Mars.

the VNIR reflectance spectra of lake sediments are strongly influenced by source sediment mineralogy and the relative proportions of different grain sizes in the sediment, which can be used to reconstruct paleoenvironmental changes on Earth and Mars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the VNIR spectral properties of phyllosilicates in lake sediment records on Earth are driven primarily by grain size, and that this is likely a key factor for interpreting the spectral properties of phylllosilicate-bearing lake sediment deposits on Mars.
the lake sedimentary record at Lake Towuti preserves the history of river incision and delta progradation during glacial and interglacial periods.
the spectral properties of the sedimentary record in lake basins on Mars can be used to reconstruct paleolake history and climate change. © 2016 The Authors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

paleolake sediment records on Earth can provide a useful analog for the development of paleoclimate models for Mars, and that VNIR reflectances spectroscopy can be an important tool for characterizing these records.

paleoclimate records in terrestrial lakes are driven by the interplay of sedimentary processes, including river incision, delta progradation, and sedimentation, which can be used to understand the evolution of lake basins on Mars.

VNIR reflectances of sedimentary phyllo-silicates can be used to infer paleoclimate conditions and reconstruct the environmental evolution of paleolakes on Earth and Mars. © 2017 American Geophysical Union.
